Since, For, and in For Duration
There are different time expressions people can use to talk about different time duration .
People work on data backup for hours or even days, but this varies according to the type of backup the person chooses.
It is time consuming and hence it's performed once in a while.
Another one is the differential backup which consists of fully backing up the information that has changed since the last full backup.

It is possible to use adverbs and prepositions to express time in different ways. In this case, you can use since, for, and in to talk about duration.

Since can be used when people want to talk about an action that started in the past, and it continues in the present. This preposition is used when you want to make the starting point of the action explicit.

Example:
I knew you were coming since last year.

For is used with a period of time. When the action has an established duration, you use this preposition. Some periods of time are ambiguous like “for a long time, for ages”, among others.

. Example:
I've been working on types of backup for two years now.

In is used when talking about months, years, and long periods of time.

Example:
In January, I will start the backup.
Types of Backups
There are different types of backups that might help people save data according to the size of information the person manages.

mong the types of backups, we can find some alike but that varies slightly. These are some basics:

A full backup is the one people perform when saving the whole data is necessary. A full copy of information is made. From this type of backup, other subsequent types of backup can be performed. The incremental backup is one of those. This one implies to back up the files that have been modified since the previous backup. The one that is pretty close to this one is the differential backup because it backs up the information that has been modified since the last full backup.

The other one is the synthetic full backup , which combines the data from full backups and incremental backups. The last one is the incremental-forever backup, which works as a regular incremental backup, but the software used allows the server to automatize the restoration process.

In most of the backup procedures, restoration is very time-consuming, especially with incremental and differential backups. However, some processes don't require extensive working periods spent on retrieving and organizing information.

images.text: <div align="justify">In data migration, there are different types of data backup that employ different times and techniques to join and connect information. When performing data movement, it's important to ponder on the time and resources as it sometimes can be an expensive process. However, it's crucial for anyone who plans to perform the backup, to know the different available techniques that will help people save time and money. People work on data backup for hours or even days, but this varies according to the type of backup the person has chosen.

<div align="justify">The first is the full backup that people use to copy full data. This backup is performed usually in a couple of days, but it all depends on the size of the data. It is time-consuming and hence it's performed occasionally. The next is an incremental backup, in which data modified after each backup is copied. Though it is less consuming than the first, it takes more time when restoring and it gets more demanding for backup operators. Another one is the differential backup which consists of fully backing up the information that has changed since the last full backup. This one is advantageous because it takes less time to restore, making unnecessary to work for hours and hours organizing pieces of backed up data.

<div align="justify">The last two are the synthetic full backup and incremental-forever backup. The first one is similar to an incremental backup but it creates full backup combining the data of full and incremental backups, of course, it reduces exponentially the restore time; the second works as a regular incremental backup, but the server automatizes the restoration process saving time and avoiding dull and repetitive procedures.
